1:
Thanks to your actions, Les Baguettes has noticed a critical flaw in its password security, and improved it significantly!

Called 'user-friendly' by the developers, the old system showed if someone else has the password you typed in use, to 'encourage creating unique passwords'. However, this also meant that an attacker could check if a password is in use by simply trying to log in with it.

Now, with the new system, Les Baguettes' users can rest assured that their passwords are safe from such attacks, as hashing and salting are incorporated in addition to password requirements (min. 8 characters, must include numbers, lower- and uppercase letters, and a special character). Great job!

You also made Britney change her password, which is quite an accomplishment! (But the story doesn't tell: to what?) The Daily Loaf was also contacted for NEVER publishing what someone has to say about their passwords in this detail EVER AGAIN!
2:
Thanks to your sharp eye, the owners were able to flag, filter, and remove these suspicious emails before a single crumb of trouble could fall into their systems. The staff now feels far more confident managing their inbox, and the bakery has implemented new protocols to keep future messages from causing a stir.

The review also served as an important reminder: even a single careless click on a link from an untrusted or misleading email can open the door to malware, credential theft, or other digital disasters. Scammers often hide harmful links behind friendly wording, familiar branding, or emotional appeals, making it all the more important to pause and inspect before clicking. 

“Thankfully Susan Supplier appears to just be our new supplier who isn’t quite used to not including links in her emails yet — instead of a vile person pretending to be one!” Lauri Leipäläpi laughed, relieved that no harm had been done. “But who knows…” Lauri added with a smirk, “maybe there really was a person willing to send us $50,000,000.00 and we just ignored her! But seriously, where could these emails come from, and why to us?”

Regardless, Lauri Leipäläpi sighed in relief, and began packing Ichirou Zennin his baguettes to send to Japan immediately.
3:
Thanks to your careful attention and investigative work, Les Baguettes has finally managed to seal up some of the messiest cracks in its digital foundations. Casual mentions, forgotten references, and half-joking technical notes had quietly revealed far more than intended, creating a situation where systems meant only for trusted hands, like the admin panel, could be influenced by those without the proper role or responsibility.

With privileges properly scoped, content integrity restored, and the last crumbs of developer overreach swept away, the bakery’s website is once again aligned with its mission: honest baking, open doors, and no hidden barriers.“Bread is meant to be shared,” the 2nd co-owner Lasse Leipäläpi said afterward. “Not gated.”

And while the front counter remains as welcoming as ever, the owners are now keenly aware that even small digital leaks left unattended can grow into much larger problems if allowed to rise unchecked.
4:
Thank you (x3) for helping out with the digital system in the backrooms of the bakery. With your help, the owners were able to find a missing secret recipe that has kept the bakery up and running until this day. The owners also had some problems with a message from a supplier that they could not simply understand because it was not meant for humans to read. Also, a lost order of a very, very important person was recovered thanks to your great actions!

Nowadays, it is crucial for companies to have functional digital systems and personnel that know how to use the systems. Very basic system knowledge can go a long way. 

“Turns out,” Lauri Leipäläpi admitted with a tired smile after all this, “that the computers and systems need just as much care as the loaves.”
